chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Bahri, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) in the Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha prayers. He said: 'Begin by saying one Takbir, then recite (the Quran), then say five Takbirs after the recitation, then bow in the seventh (Takbir). Then stand up, recite (again), then say four Takbirs, then bow in the fifth (Takbir).'

key_terms.السَّابِعَةِ: The seventh (referring to the count of Takbirs)
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs are recited in the Eid prayers before and after the Quranic recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific ritual structure of Eid prayers as narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), detailing the precise count of Takbirat in each rak'ah. It establishes the Shia jurisprudential practice of reciting seven Takbirat in the first rak'ah (before and after Fatiha) and five in the second, distinguishing it from other schools of thought. This narration serves as a primary textual basis for the legal rulings regarding the performance of these communal festivals.
